vehicle.mass_note: Measured on the setup patch with wheel adapters, 75 kg driver and 35 kg fuel; the adapters cancel in the ratios.

corner_weights.note: Measured on the setup patch including adapters; RR is total - FL - FR - RL.

vehicle.yaw_inertia_note: Estimated as Iz = m x a x b (bicycle-model approximation), error about 10-20 %; replace with a homologation value when available.
vehicle.steering_ratio_note: Read from the steering ratio lookup table at centre wheel travel and zero steering stroke; treated as constant (Level 1).
vehicle.cog_note: From the static weight distribution: a = L x rear_fraction, b = L x front_fraction.
vehicle.cog_height_note: Order-of-magnitude placeholder, not sourced; replace with a team figure.
vehicle.track_width_note: Order-of-magnitude placeholder, not sourced; replace with a team figure.

aero.air_density_note: ISA sea-level standard value (Level 1); no session weather correction is implemented.
aero.lift_coeff_sign_convention: cl < 0 means downforce, cl > 0 means lift (standard aerodynamic Cl sign, not a downforce-positive convention); verified computationally against estimate_vertical_loads. The first real Cl entry must be negative.
aero.lift_coeff_note: Placeholder 0.0 (Level 1): the aero load term is zero, so Fz underestimates both axle loads at speed but not the front/rear balance. Sign as in fz_aero = -0.5 rho v^2 A Cl, Cl < 0 = downforce (after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal)); a first real Cl must make the axle-load sum rise with v^2 on a straight.
aero.cross_track_area_note: Frontal area (Level 1, literature), used for drag with longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff; the lift model shares it but stays zero while lift_coeff = 0.
aero.cross_track_area_derived_from: A = 2.0 m^2 for a generic race car of touring-car size (Trzesniowski 2019), cross-checked against 1.78 m^2 for a Porsche 911 Carrera road car (Katz 1995); no team value exists.
aero.diff_cog_x_note: Centre-of-pressure to CoG longitudinal offset, not sourced; inert while lift_coeff = 0. A value of 0 means no front/rear aero balance shift.

stability_estimation._comment_yaw_rate_unit: Logged yaw rate is in rpm; 2 x pi / 60 = 0.10472 converts to rad/s. The parser checks the declared unit of sclu_yaw_rate and stops on a mismatch instead of scaling by the wrong factor.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: Cornering-stiffness window floors: cs_min_window_s = 0.1 s is the chair value; 0.2 s gave the same results on the development data, so there is no reason to deviate.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor for slow logs (e.g. 20 Hz), where the time floor would give fewer samples than a robust two-parameter least-squares fit needs.
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: Locality cap for cornering-stiffness window growth in track metres, so it means the same in slow and fast corners: 1.5 x the median natural rear window. Where corners are closer than this a window can reach into the neighbour; floors not met within the cap give NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: A per-phase CS_ratio median needs at least this many finite samples, so it is not set by one or two extreme readings; otherwise NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: The entry_1_brake stability statistic needs the same sample count as CS and a front brake pressure above this floor; 3 bar lies between transient noise at full throttle and real braking (above about 13 bar).
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: derived on the development data (see thesis)
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: Common grid rate = min(target_sample_rate_hz, slowest native rate of the fast CS channels); below min_sample_rate_hz the run is refused, exactly at it the run is marked channel-limited. Time windows are converted to samples at the grid rate; apex_half_window_samples is still a sample count.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: Which beta feeds the cornering-stiffness ratio and yaw-moment stability. 'ekf_auto_pacejka' (default) uses the per-session tyre fit and observer; 'kinematic' is the universal fallback. Verdict thresholds are calibrated for one source; another source is marked [UNCAL].
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source_auto_modes: 'ekf_auto_pacejka': fit the session tyre curve, run the NIS gate and use the observer beta only if the gate passes or warns and the fit is not degenerate; otherwise kinematic beta with the fallback reason recorded.
stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: 'static' = static, aero and load-transfer model; 'measured' (default) = damper-based wheel loads with reconstruction and static fallback, which also feed the tyre fit, the observer and Fy/Fz under the default fit. Without damper channels both give identical results.
stability_estimation.vertical_load_source_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: apex_3 is one instant +/- apex_half_window_samples and is too short for a cornering-stiffness window, so its CS is read over +/- cs_apex_region_half_length_m around the apex: 25 m covers the typical CS dip without reaching the next corner or straight.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Yaw-moment stability estimator after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal), with the chair defaults; changing any of the six values requires re-deriving the classification thresholds.
stability_estimation.kerb_dilation_s_derived_from: Kerb mask padding of +/- 0.1 s, given in seconds so the physical padding is the same at 50 and 100 Hz grid rate; premise checked on the development data (see thesis).
stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

nis_gate._comment: NIS tyre-mismatch gate (modules/observer.py). The window length and the NIS band are set here only; the thresholds were derived on the default fit over the development sessions.
nis_gate.nis_window_s_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
nis_gate.threshold_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

tyre_fit_auto._comment: Tunables of the per-session Pacejka tyre fit (fit L) with observer validation. P0, beta_hard_bound and the interim yaw-rate R seed come from the earlier observer; the seed is used only in the interim run that fixes R_ay first. The fit population is limited to a per-session speed percentile window (fit_speed_window_pct, null = off), which drops the fastest, mostly straight-line samples like the speed bands of the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal).
tyre_fit_auto._comment_q_reference_rate_hz: Reference rate of the per-step process-noise variances: Q is scaled by q_reference_rate_hz / grid rate (first-order discretisation of white process noise), so the variance per second is the same at 50 and 100 Hz. A convention, not a tunable.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_l_observer: Observer process noise Q is computed per session as a held-over-step upper bound from the fit force residual (Level 2), propagated to beta_dot and r_dot, diagonal (Villano et al. 2021; Bechtloff ch. 5). The observer resets on the hard bound only.
tyre_fit_auto.l_q_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
tyre_fit_auto._comment_l_straights: Steering-defined straights on which the session ay sensor noise is measured (R_ay floor, modules/observer.py). Tier B segmentation from steering and speed only: steering-centre histogram bin, sigma-factor thresholds on a robust sigma, a moving average before differentiating steering, and the longest minimum duration that still leaves enough segments on every analysis lap.
tyre_fit_auto.l_straight_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
tyre_fit_auto.fit_speed_window_pct_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
tyre_fit_auto._comment_fit_density_bin_rad: Inverse-density weights on the signed slip angle of the fit population, weight = 1 / (samples in the bin), so the even data distribution of Goblirsch et al. 2025 holds. Tier B; the bin width is a resolution choice, not a literature value.
tyre_fit_auto.fit_density_bin_rad_derived_from: Resolution choice carried over from an earlier fit variant; not tuned to data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_fit_long_util_max: Braking samples whose utilisation |Fx_axle| / Fz_axle exceeds this value leave that axle fit population, so the pure-slip curve is fitted on near-pure-slip data (Farroni 2016; Farroni et al. 2018). By the friction circle (Pacejka 2006) the lateral capacity loss at 0.3 is about 2-2.5 % for mu 1.4-1.6; traction samples are kept and the observer runs on every sample. Fx from the Goblirsch et al. 2025 split, measured Fz.
tyre_fit_auto.fit_long_util_max_derived_from: Friction-circle bound on the lateral capacity loss, about 2-2.5 % at mu 1.4-1.6 (Pacejka 2006); not tuned to data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_mu_demo_percentile: mu per axle = this percentile of |Fy| / Fz on the fit population: demonstrated utilisation, a lower bound of true friction. Tier B percentile, fixed before results were seen. Anchors: Farroni et al. 2018 (peak bounded by the maximum acquired forces); Acosta Reche et al. 2018 (conservative grip estimate); chair performance_analysis tooling (internal), mue_effective.
tyre_fit_auto.mu_demo_percentile_derived_from: Fixed before any result was seen; not tuned to data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_r_sweep_selection: Level 1 calibration tunables. R is selected on the ay NIS exceedance only: the in-band grid point nearest the band centre whose sign-check fraction reaches sign_check_marginal_fraction, else the defaults with status at most marginal. The yaw exceedance stays far above any NIS band because the yaw innovation is dominated by single-track model mismatch, so yaw is logged but not selected on; the defaults are the setting chosen on all sweep sessions of the development data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_yaw_mismatch_ceiling: Level 1 calibration tunable. The yaw NIS exceedance reflects single-track model mismatch, not noise calibration, so it never makes a fit degenerate; above this ceiling it caps the status at marginal. Set well above the healthy range seen on the development data (about 0.2-0.5).
tyre_fit_auto._comment_status: ok / marginal / degenerate boundaries of the fit status.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_plausibility_gate: Tyre-curve plausibility gate. min_alpha_span_deg: p1-p99 span of the fit slip angles (excitation). stiffness_min_npr / stiffness_max_npr: linear axle stiffness band in N/rad (magnitudes after Bechtloff), used as the CS reference band when the CS runs on Fy.
tyre_fit_auto.mu_ceiling_edge_u_derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)
tyre_fit_auto.tyre_fit_mode_default_note: Fit L (literature_bounded) is the only analysis path; the key stays so the [UNCAL] marker and the threshold calibration tag can compare against it.

longitudinal_stiffness._comment: Axle Fx from the longitudinal force balance at the CoG (modules/loads.py) with drag and rolling resistance; input to the axle force split of the fit and to the floor-event attributes. The block name is historical.
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_note: Level 1, literature: with vehicle.aero.cross_track_area_m2 = 2.0 the longitudinal balance gains 0.5 rho c_D A v^2 (c_D A = 1.0 m^2).
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_derived_from: c_D = 0.50, midpoint of production-based GT race cars of about 1990 (Katz 1995); no team value exists, and a modern GT3 car likely has more drag.
longitudinal_stiffness.rolling_resistance_coeff_note: Not sourced; zero is a documented first-order simplification, since a slick tyre rolling resistance is one to two orders of magnitude below drag and traction forces at racing speed.

wheel_loads._comment: Per-wheel Fz from pushrod force and suspension travel (modules/loads.py; Segers ch. 9/10): Level 4 per corner where log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are valid, static split (Level 1) as per-corner fallback. A session whose mean straight-line damper axle total falls below plausibility_min_static_fraction x m g uses the static split instead; damper zeros from an event entry are checked with offset-independent slopes (zero_validation).
wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_note: Level 1 default (zero). log_dms_dam_* is already logged in N, so an offset here would be a zero-load calibration, not a unit conversion; event-specific gauge zeros come from channels.json event_zero_entries, and the straight-line total-load check tests the zeroing.
wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_note: Level 1, not independently sourced: typical per-wheel unsprung mass of a GT3-class car. Feeds the unsprung lateral-transfer term, which acts through the upright and tyre and is added on top of the damper-derived sprung force.
wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_note: Level 1 estimate: static circumference / (2 pi) from the team-supplied circumferences (front 2140 mm, rear 2210 mm), not corrected for the few-percent smaller loaded radius. Used only as the unsprung transfer arm.
wheel_loads.roll_centre_note: Level 1 estimate: roll_center_mm of the baseline kinematic variant in config/car_data.json (FS15 front, RS25 rear), not confirmed against the variant fitted. Used for the geometric sprung lateral-transfer term only; the elastic part is already in the measured pushrod force and must not be added twice.
wheel_loads.arb_motion_ratio_approximation_note: Approximation: car_data.json has no ARB-linkage motion ratio, so modules/loads.py uses the damper motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel of the same axle for the ARB as well.
wheel_loads.arb_position_default_note: Level 1 default ARB blade position (1-7) for both axles. It only changes the left/right split of an axle damper load; axle totals and every result are independent of it.
wheel_loads.bump_rubber_note: Not modelled: a wheel on its bump rubber reads an underestimated load, because only the spring/damper and ARB paths are decomposed. The bump_stop_curve in car_data.json is not used.
wheel_loads.aero_front_fraction_note: Level 1 estimate, not an aero-balance measurement: the front share of the session-fitted aero coefficient (Level 2). From per-corner straight-line damper residual fits a + b v^2 on the development data (see thesis), b front 0.39 vs rear 1.18 N/(m/s)^2, giving 0.25; roll-transfer terms cancel in an axle total. To be confirmed by wind tunnel or CFD; the value used is reported with every reconstruction.
wheel_loads.plausibility_min_static_fraction_derived: derived on the development data (see thesis)
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_travel_mm_derived_f: derived on the development data (see thesis)

zero_validation.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_force_N_derived_fro: derived on the development data (see thesis)

corner_trace_display._comment: Plot only: how far the corner trace window extends beyond the phase bracket for approach and exit context, clamped to the lap. Phase bands still cover the five phases only.
corner_trace_display.cs_ls_panel_y_range_note: Fixed y-range of the CS ratio panels, so numerically unstable windows cannot stretch the axis and hide the meaningful 0..1 region; set from the observed CS_ratio range plus headroom. Out-of-range samples are not drawn.
corner_trace_display.default_laps_shown_note: From an all-laps analysis the fastest N valid laps of the corner start checked, the rest stay available; N = 5 avoids overlapping colours and stays inside the 10-colour palette. Tier C UI default.
corner_trace_display.kerb_exclusion_display_note: One switch for every CS trace, histogram and tyre-curve scatter in the app and the figure exports, so app and thesis figures agree: grey (default) draws kerb-affected samples grey, exclude leaves them out, off draws them normally. Kerb-affected = inside the kerb mask or near_strike. Presentation only; no computed result changes.

cs_envelope._comment: Cross-lap envelope (core/display.py) drawn as two thin lines on the CS and stability panels over all analysis laps of the corner, with the selected lap on top. Display only.
cs_envelope.percentiles_derived_from: p10 / p90 rather than min / max, so one wild lap does not set the band.
cs_envelope.min_laps_derived_from: Display floor: fewer than 3 analysis laps at a grid point gives no band there.

classification._comment: Corner-verdict thresholds. STRONG = p10 and MODERATE = p30 of the worst-lap, worst-phase corner CS ratios per axle over the development pool: relative ranks for this estimator and car, never taken from the chair. Physical statements come from separate labels (ratio < 0: axle force falling while slip grows); rear saturation reduces the stability margin (Hoffman et al. 2008). verdict_stability_margin marks a verdict MARGINAL when its value lies within cs_margin of a threshold (covers the vehicle inputs only, not the observer); an axle counts as limiting when its CS ratio is below minus cs_boundary_margin_front / _rear (combined observer and vehicle-input uncertainty).

STRONG_CSF.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

STRONG_CSR.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

MODERATE_CSF.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

MODERATE_CSR.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

stab_neg_thresh_Nm_per_deg.derived_from: Sign criterion of Werner 2021 sec. 2.2.3: dMz/dbeta < 0 is open-loop unstable; a boundary, not a criticality threshold, since skilled drivers operate there.

verdict_stability_margin.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

cs_boundary_margin_front.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

cs_boundary_margin_rear.derived_from: derived on the development data (see thesis)

setup_engine._comment: Setup engine (modules/setup_engine.py). A corner-phase symptom counts when it appears in more than min_repeat_fraction of the corner valid laps and in at least min_repeat_laps laps (Tier B). The session share of corners with a counted symptom is always reported; the session recommendation comes from session_vote.
setup_engine.repeat_derived_from: Present in a majority of the valid laps, at least 2, so a single lap cannot create a symptom.
setup_engine.session_share_threshold_derived_from: Kept null: the session share is computed and reported, but no recommendation is drawn from it.
setup_engine.damper_step_derived_from: Team practice: dampers are the race-weekend fine-tuning lever, so the 1-click fine step is used; larger steps are test-day advice (TE).

session_vote._comment: Session recommendation (Tier B aggregation): each counted corner symptom votes for its candidate levers with weight severity_weight x k / n (k of n valid laps show it); opposite directions of the same lever subtract, and net support <= 0 is never recommended. Driver-only symptoms (|feedback| >= 4, no data support) vote with driver_only_weight.
session_vote.derived_from: Set as a simple, explainable aggregation rule; not tuned to data.

limit_events._comment: Floor events (modules/limit_events.py), display and record only: contiguous runs of the CS ratio below the pure-lateral floor -0.53 with measured attributes, no bridging or minimum duration; never a verdict or recommendation input.
limit_events.recurrence_radius_m_derived_from: An event recurs when another analysis lap has an event on the same axle at the same corner with its minimum within this lap distance.

accuracy_levels._comment: Accuracy per quantity: 1 = config default, 2 = session measurement, 3 = logged sensor, 4 = lookup table. Per node: static level, source and capped_by ('chained-constant: <name>' = a Level 1 constant in its derivation; 'provenance-assumption: <name>' = an unverifiable assumption about the channel; null = neither). modules/accuracy_resolution.py resolves the leaf nodes per outing; derived nodes follow their caps, bounded by the method ceiling where one exists (e.g. m x a x b for yaw inertia).

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); resolves to Level 4 (manufacturer steering table in car_data.json) when that local file is present, with the wheel angle interpolated from the wheel-angle column (mean of both front wheels). Vehicle parameterisation, not a deviation from the chair.

longitudinal_force_split.source: Fx = m x ax + drag + rolling resistance (estimate_longitudinal_forces), same construction as the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); split to the axles by measured axle load in the tyre fit (Goblirsch 2025, Eq. 9)
longitudinal_force_split.note: Drag Level 1 from literature: c_D A = 0.50 x 2.0 = 1.0 m^2; rolling resistance stays 0 (documented approximation).

sideslip_angle.source: per-session Pacejka fit with observer, gated (modules/tyre_fit_auto.py, sideslip_source = 'ekf_auto_pacejka'); falls back to kinematic integration with washout (estimate_sideslip) when the NIS gate fails or the fit is degenerate
sideslip_angle.note: Level 1, because the fit is a per-session model, not a measured, logged or lookup source; fallback and gate outcome are recorded in the analysis result. A GPS-course Level 3 path was not viable on this data.

speed.note: GPS speed is a diagnostic cross-check only: ecu_speed reads about 1.2 % below GPS, a candidate rolling-radius correction that is not applied because it would change an estimator input.

yaw_rate.source: sclu_yaw_rate logged channel, exact rpm-to-radps unit conversion

steering_angle.source: log_asteer logged channel (steering-wheel angle), converted with the constant steering_ratio at Level 1 or the manufacturer wheel-angle map at Level 4; takes the resolved level of steering_ratio

lateral_acc.source: log_acc_y logged channel, exact g-to-mps2 unit conversion

wheelbase_m.note: Fixed chassis dimension known to design tolerance; Level 1 by convention.

vertical_load_split.source: axle Fz from static + aero + longitudinal-transfer decomposition (estimate_vertical_loads), same construction as the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal)

per_wheel_load_split.source: per-axle lateral-transfer split (estimate_vertical_loads), same construction as the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); not a roll-stiffness apportionment
per_wheel_load_split.note: Static split only. With vertical_load_source = measured the level is recorded per sample: 'damper' = Level 4 (logged sensor + motion-ratio table); damper loads with an event zero entry (channels.json event_zero_entries) are Level 4 with a Level 2 zero.

wheel_load_damper.source: pushrod force + motion ratio + ARB + unsprung and geometric lateral-transfer decomposition (modules/loads.py) per corner where log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are valid (Segers ch. 9/10)
wheel_load_damper.capped_by: chained-constant: wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_front/rear_kg, wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.roll_centre_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, car_data.json motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel/arb tables
wheel_load_damper.note: Per corner: a corner with a missing or failed damper or travel channel falls back to the Level 1 static split for that corner alone, recorded per sample.

wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.source: quasi-static axle total (fz_f_N / fz_r_N) minus the damper-measured mate on the same axle (modules/loads.py), used only where exactly one corner of an axle is invalid (Segers modal-decomposition method)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.capped_by: chained-constant: vertical_load_split (cog_height_m, aero lift_coeff/cross_track_area_m2/diff_cog_x_m -- the axle-total half of this method), wheel_load_damper (the measured-mate half)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.note: Level 1 although it uses three real sensors: the level records provenance, and the axle total carries the Level 1 aero and CoG-height placeholders. Tried after the damper path and before the static split. Limits: a single-wheel event at the reconstructed corner is invisible, the warp mode is unobservable, and two invalid corners on one axle fall through to the static split.
